subject: Astronomy & Space
title: Newton's Universal Gravitation
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Newton's Universal Gravitation.

hook.text: Isaac Newton unified the heavens and the Earth. The same force that drops an apple curves the Moon's orbit.

buildup.text: His law of universal gravitation says every mass attracts every other mass. The strength fades with distance squared.

discovery.text: Newton proved that Kepler's laws are consequences of gravity. One equation explained all planetary motion.

twist.text: Newton invented calculus to solve these problems. He published it in 1687—and then feuded with Leibniz over credit.

climax.text: His work dominated physics for over 200 years—until Einstein showed gravity is actually curved spacetime.

punchline.text: One force, one law. Apples and moons obey the same equation.

quiz.question: What did Newton's law of universal gravitation unify?
options: The force governing objects on Earth and the motion of celestial bodies
The orbits of comets and the behavior of light

details.summary: Isaac Newton's law of universal gravitation (1687) states that every mass attracts every other mass with a force proportional to their masses and inversely proportional to the square of their distance.
details.whyItMatters: Newton unified terrestrial and celestial physics — showing the same force that pulls an apple down also keeps the Moon in orbit. This was the first universal physical law and remains one of science's greatest intellectual achievements.
takeaways: Every mass attracts every other mass through gravity
The force decreases with the square of the distance
Newton unified the physics of Earth and the heavens

faq.question: Did an apple really fall on Newton's head?
faq.answer: The falling apple story is partially true but embellished. Newton himself told the story of seeing an apple fall, which prompted him to wonder if the same force extended to the Moon. But there's no evidence it hit his head.

faq.question: How did Newton's gravity explain Kepler's laws?
faq.answer: Newton mathematically proved that an inverse-square gravitational force naturally produces elliptical orbits (Kepler's first law), equal-area sweeping (second law), and the period-distance relationship (third law). Kepler described how — Newton explained why.
